texts.facts: Vide this judgment, I shall dispose of the state's appeal challenging the order dated 27.03.2018 ("the impugned order" in short) of Ld. Adjudicating Officer/Additional District Magistrate (Central) ("ADM" in short), New Delhi whereby, the application under Rule 3.1.1(3) of The Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011("FSSR" in short) filed by FSO was dismissed observing that the respondents deserve benefit of doubt in view of contradictory reports of Food Analyst and of Central Food Laboratory(CFL). 2.0 Briefly stating, the facts as per appeal are that : (i) on 29.12.2014, Food Safety Officer ("FSO" in short), purchased sample of "Pasteurized Full Cream Milk" from Sh. Satish Sharma/respondent no.1. The sample consisted of approx. 2 x 1 litre taken from sealed poly pack (ready for sale), bearing label declaration "Pasteurized Full Cream Milk" on it; (ii) the sample of Pasteurized Full Cream Milk was taken after proper mixing with the help of clean & dry measure by rotating in all possible directions i.e. up & Food Safety Officer vs Sh.Satish Sharma & Ors. Food Safety Officer vs Satish Sharma on 23 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198921252/ 2 :: 4 :: down, clock wise and anticlockwise several times. The sample of pasteurized full cream milk was divided into four equal parts then and there by putting into four clean and dry glass bottles and 40 drops of formalin was added in each bottle with the help of clean and dry dropper. Each bottle containing the sample was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to the provisions of FSS Act and Rules/ Regulations framed thereunder; (iii) one counterpart of the sample under sealed cover was sent to Food Analyst. Other two counterparts were deposited with Designated Officer. As the FBO did not make a request to send the fourth counter part for analysis from NABL Acreedited Laboratory, the fourth sealed counterpart was also deposited with the Designated Officer; (iv) the Food Analyst vide his report dated 12.01.2015 opined "The sample is substandard because milk solids not fat is less than the prescribed minimum limit of 9.0%; Food Safety Officer vs Sh.Satish Sharma & Ors. :: 5 :: (v) the Designated Officer concerned sent a copy of the Food Analyst report to the respondent's giving them an opportunity to file an appeal against the report of the Food Analyst u/S 46(4) FSS Act for sending one part of the same to the Referral Lab, if so desired. An appeal against Food Analyst's report was preferred. Accordingly, one sample was sent to Director, Food Safety and Analytical Quality Control Laboratory, C/o CFTRI, Mysore; (vi) the Director Referral Food Laboratory, Mysore vide Certificate dated 09.04.2015 reported that sample is substandard as defined u/S 3(1)(zx) FSS Act and does not conform to the standards laid down for full cream milk under the provisions of The Food Safety and Standards(Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011("FSS(FPS & FA) Regulations" in short) thereof, as "Milk fat content falls below the minimum standard limit"; (vii) in view of the above, an application/ complaint Food Safety Officer vs Sh.Satish Sharma & Ors. :: 6 :: under rule 3.1.1(3) FSS Rules was filed by FSO before the Ld. ADM; Food Safety Officer vs Satish Sharma on 23 May, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198921252/ 3
texts.arguments: 3.0 The appellant /FSO has challenged the impugned order on the grounds that the Ld. ADM failed to appreciate that in terms of the provisions contained in Section 47(c) of FSS Act read with Rule 2.4.6 of FSS Rules, 2011, the report of Referral Food Laboratory is final and has to be given precedence over the report of Food Analyst; and that the Ld. ADM even failed to appreciate the law as laid by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Delhi Administration Vs. Vidya Gupta [Crl. Appeal No. 625/18]. 4.0 The respondents have sought dismissal of the appeal pleading that the Ld. ADM rightly acquitted the respondents giving benefit of doubt to them in view of variation in Reports of Food Analyst and Referral Food Laboratory. 4.1 Ld. counsel for the respondents also argued that in case this court is inclined to [LEAKAGE_MASK] the impugned order, they would Food Safety Officer vs Sh.Satish Sharma & Ors. :: 7 :: like to point out that the Ld. ADM failed to record any findings on other contentions raised by them before him vide their reply, including their request for cross examination of FSO. 4.2 Ld. Counsel for the respondents no. 4 & 5 also argued that the Ld. ADM did not refer to any of their contentions viz. the procedure adopted by RFL (IS:1224,1977) for arriving at the fat content in the milk was gerber method and was not proper, as has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court. Further, even addition of excess preservative/ 40 drops of formalin rendered the milk sub standard.
